pr_title: Highlight invalid playlist items during room creation
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/15643.

Not 100% on the UX here (maybe they should be automatically removed) but this seems okay?

issue_context.title: Creating a playlist with beatmaps that aren't available online can be confusing
issue_context.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/ppy/osu/discussions/15359
Originally posted by **TheFantasticLoki** October 29, 2021 When creating a playlist and a map is added that is not submitted, the error should show more than Beatmap not found: 0,0,0 It should show the name of the map at the very least as no way to identify the problem map. This is only compounded by the fact there is no easy way to filter not submitted maps like there was in stable by typing status=not [Screenshot](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/639463329709948928/903552943935070218/unknown.png)
A quick fix for this could place a red border around the items which are invalid, or just tint the whole playlist item red. Then the user could go about removing the items.

review_comments:
If after an item being marked invalid another valid item is selected, the invalid red border disappears:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/142062897-a34856d9-a7bd-46b1-b823-a44cb3cffac9.mp4

Given that the invalid item is unclickable, that seems not intentional.
Is this a possible scenario in gameplay?
I've added logic to make this work more as expected, though I'm not sure it will ever be seen.
As to whether this could be seen, I tested and could break it in game too. Unless I'm very confused, the initial room creation subscreen didn't/doesn't disable selection.
The more you know... I've never actually selected an item there because... it does nothing 😅.

Not sure if it's just me but I'm not really getting the point of exposing as `IBindable<bool>` if `MarkInvalid()` is going to be a public method anyhow. Feels a little overdone at this point, I guess.
I didn't want to allow it to set set to valid again, since I'm not handling that scenario.
I'm not against changing it, your call.
Ideally web would provide a more structured error than this that doesn't require de-stringifying, but this works for now I guess...

Already discussed with web team, this is best we have and likely won't change for the foreseeable future (the only more structure error web uses is `form_errors` which only gives the erroring property in addition, no json structure or anything).
Not sure that this code path is ever reached, `OnClick` already seems to disallow selection preemptively. But I guess it shouldn't hurt to have it just in case either way.
Not sure whether this ordering change does anything, although it does feel more correct...
See https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/15648/commits/e78c5d0858479780a8bafaac5462533f5230738d, explained in the commit message.
